problem_statement: The paper frames anomaly detection as the task of identifying data points or patterns that deviate from normal behavior, and it treats one-class classification as the setting where only normal data are available for training. classical_difficulty: The paper says kernel-based SVDD has poor computational scaling because it requires constructing and manipulating the kernel matrix, and it also needs support vectors to be stored in memory. More generally, it says AD is harder than binary classification because anomalies are rare, so training has limited label information and must use unsupervised learning.
